lines.text: See that tiny hole in your airplane window? It's the reason the window holds.
Up at cruising height, the air inside the cabin is pushing outward, hard.
On one window, that's about half a ton.
So the window isn't one pane. It's three.
The inner one is just a scratch shield.
The outer pane takes the whole load. The middle pane has the hole.
Air leaks through it, so the middle pane feels nothing... it's resting.
But if the outer pane ever cracks... the middle one takes over.
Bonus: the hole lets moisture out, which helps keep your view clear.
So that tiny hole? It's the backup plan you're sitting next to.
